name: Activity Timeline
why: Shows, at a glance, how the agent's time was really spent: long stretches of captcha-solving, account sign-up, and money-hunting, with the actual exploit work only a thin sliver at the very end. It makes the "where did 10.5 hours go" finding visible and lets the analyst click any point to jump to that record.
arrangement:
Unit: One record, keyed by the `index` field and placed at its `timestamp`, carrying the "tactic" label (captcha / signup / money / exploit / infra / other). 2064 records span 2026-07-18 01:02 to 11:28 UTC.
Overview: A horizontal time axis (01:00 to 11:30) with one lane per tactic value. Each record is a mark in its lane at its timestamp, colored by tactic. The viewer can see the dense captcha/signup/money bands through the middle, the thin "exploit" marks clustered at the end, and the context-compaction boundary (~07:30, the two Human records) drawn as a vertical line. An optional density band per lane shows records-per-10-minutes.
Zoom: Drag to zoom a time range; click a mark to open that record (its reasoning or tool call + result). Hover shows index, timestamp, activity, and the first line of the record.
Filter: By tactic value (the label), by tool, by time range, and by the Labels pane filter. Selecting one activity dims the others.
Details: On demand: the record's index and file line, full timestamp, tool name, and the reasoning/command text, so a click moves from the timeline to the exact evidence.
